ideas.title: Prompt Compression Studio
ideas.summary: Paste an overly long prompt, set a target token budget, and watch Claude trim it down with a live diff showing exactly what was cut and how much money you'll save per 1000 API calls.
ideas.description: A web app where you paste an overly long prompt or conversation history and specify a target token budget. Claude analyzes and rewrites the content, preserving the critical instructions and examples while removing redundancy, over-explanation, and filler. A side-by-side diff shows exactly what was cut, a meter shows the token reduction percentage, and an estimated cost savings calculator tells you how much you would save per 1000 API calls at current pricing.
keyFeatures: Paste or type any prompt and set a target token budget with a slider
Claude-powered compression that preserves intent while eliminating redundancy
Side-by-side diff highlighting removed and rewritten passages in color
Token count and cost savings calculator supporting Claude, GPT-4, and Gemini pricing tiers
One-click copy of the compressed prompt with an option to iterate further
ideas.techStack: React + Vite + Tailwind, Claude API (claude-sonnet-4-6), tiktoken or Anthropic token counter, Flask proxy for API key safety
ideas.whyInteresting: Every developer who works with LLMs eventually hits token limits or a surprisingly large invoice -- this tool makes prompt optimization fast and visual, and teaching yourself to write tighter prompts is a genuinely transferable skill.
ideas.inspiredBy: GitHub trending June 2026 discussion on LLM context limits and MiniMax M3's 1M-token context window launch (https://github.com/trending)

ideas.title: Assignment Scaffolder
ideas.summary: Describe a programming assignment in plain English and get back a ready-to-distribute package: starter code with TODO stubs, a rubric, tiered hints, and autograder-ready test cases.
ideas.description: An instructor-facing web tool where you describe a programming assignment in plain English and Claude generates a complete, ready-to-distribute assignment package: starter code with strategic TODO stubs, a detailed rubric with point breakdowns, autograder-friendly test cases, and a set of tiered hints that progressively reveal the solution path. Everything is exported as a downloadable zip so the instructor can push it directly to a course GitHub org.
keyFeatures: Natural language assignment description form with optional constraints (language, libraries, time limit)
Claude generates starter code with TODOs at pedagogically useful breakpoints
Structured rubric output with point weights across functionality, style, testing, and documentation
Progressive hint set (3-5 levels) that guides students without giving away the answer
Autograder-ready test suite in pytest or Jest exported alongside the starter code
One-click zip download for the full assignment package
ideas.techStack: React + Vite + Tailwind, Flask backend, Claude API (claude-sonnet-4-6), Supabase for template storage
ideas.whyInteresting: Writing good scaffolded assignments is one of the most time-consuming parts of teaching CS -- a tool that turns a one-sentence description into a publish-ready package could save instructors hours per assignment.
ideas.inspiredBy: HN 'Ask HN: What developer tool do you wish existed in 2026?' (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46345827) and n8n's 2026 AI agent development tools report

ideas.title: Agentic Study Buddy Network
ideas.summary: Students build a multi-agent tutoring system where specialized domain agents hand off conversations between each other, maintain a shared memory of what the student knows, and visualize their growing knowledge as an interactive graph.
ideas.description: Students build a multi-agent tutoring system where specialized Claude-powered study buddy agents each own a topic domain (data structures, algorithms, systems, etc.) and can hand off a student to a peer agent when the conversation shifts domains. A shared Supabase memory store tracks what the student has already mastered so no agent re-explains known concepts. The student-facing interface is a single chat window that seamlessly transitions between agents, and a dashboard shows the student a graph of their growing knowledge map.
keyFeatures: At least three domain agents with their own system prompts that route conversations based on topic detection
Handoff protocol where the sending agent writes a context summary that the receiving agent reads
Shared persistent memory in Supabase recording mastered concepts, common mistakes, and last-session summary
Student-facing knowledge graph (Cytoscape.js) that updates after each session
Instructor panel showing aggregate knowledge gaps across the class by topic node
Evaluation harness that tests correct handoff detection and memory retrieval
ideas.techStack: Python FastAPI or Flask for agent orchestration, Claude API (claude-sonnet-4-6), Supabase, React + Vite + Tailwind + Cytoscape.js
ideas.whyInteresting: Building this teaches multi-agent architecture, memory design, and context management all at once in a domain students care about, and the finished product is something they can actually use in their own coursework.
ideas.inspiredBy: GitHub trending repo msitarzewski/agency-agents (specialized AI agency platform) and Hugging Face smolagents library multi-agent patterns (https://github.com/trending)
